newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DAMPHOUSSE LIFTS CANADIENS PAST WHALERS WITH HAT TRICK.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DAMPHOUSSE LIFTS CANADIENS PAST WHALERS WITH HAT TRICK.

text.p: Vincent Damphousse completed his ninth career hat trick with just four seconds left in regulation to lift the Montreal Canadiens to a 5-4 victory over the Hartford Whalers on Monday.

With the game apparently headed for overtime, Mark Recchi backhanded a clearing pass off the boards and Damphousse picked it up in the neutral zone. He carried into the Hartford zone, faked a pass and flipped a wrist shot that tipped in off goaltender Jason Muzzatti's glove for his third goal of the night and 19th of the season.
Damphousse had tied the game less than two minutes earlier when he poked home a rebound of Peter Popovic's shot with 1:53 to go.
"I'm driving to the net. I'm playing a lot better, I'm doing a lot of things better," said Damphousse, who has nine goals and two assists in his last six games.
"I've got more feel, more jump, more energy," added Damphousse, who scored his 300th career goal early in the second period to give Montreal a 3-2 lead.
Andrew Cassels scored twice for the Whalers, who took a 4-3 lead at 5:18 of the third when Sami Kapanen poked the puck past goalie Jocelyn Thibault on a goalmouth scramble.
"When Hartford went ahead 4-3, all the players on the bench said let's get going," Montreal coach Mario Tromblay said.

In New York, Mike Richter made 38 saves to extend his personal unbeaten streak to 16 games and Adam Graves scored a powerplay goal late in the second period as the Rangers rallied to tie the Colorado Avalanche 2-2.
Richter stopped all 30 shots he faced after the first period. Richter's 11-game winning streak was snapped, but he is 14-0-2 since a November 23 loss.
Bill Berg also scored for New York, which overcame a two-goal, first-period deficit.

Keith Jones and Jon Klemm scored powerplay goals in a 93-second span midway through the first period for Colorado. Jones scored at 11:16 as the Avalanche skated with a two-man advantage. Klemm then beat Richter with one Ranger still in the penalty box.
Patrick Roy made 30 saves for Colorado, which is unbeaten in their last seven (5-0-2).
In Ottawa, Alexander Selivanov had a goal and an assist and Bill Houlder scored a key insurance goal early in the third period as the Tampa Bay Lightning held off the Senators 4-3.
Daymond Langkow and Shawn Burr also scored for Tampa Bay, which escaped last place in the Atlantic Division.

Houlder scored his first goal of the season 1:43 into the third to extend the Tampa Bay lead to 4-1. But Ottawa's Lance Pitlick beat goaltender Rick Tabaracci with a wrist shot from the right point just 29 seconds later.
Houlder's goal proved the game winner after Randy Cunneyworth deflected a Janne Laukkanen slapper past Tabaracci to make it a one-goal game.
In Anaheim, Pavel Bure scored two goals, including one of Vancouver's two short-handed tallies, and Mike Sillinger added a goal and two assists to lead the Canucks to a 5-1 rout of the Mighty Ducks.
Bure, who has five goals in his last three games, snapped a 1-1 tie with his 15th goal 6:17 into second period.

Sillinger extended the lead to 3-1 with a short-handed goal at 17:12 as Vancouver scored five unanswered goals after Teemu Selanne opened the scoring for Anaheim with his 22nd goal just 40 seconds into the contest.
Kirk McLean made 30 saves for Vancouver.
